securityPosture.closedAllowlist: A fixed set of 7 named fixture IDs (A-VERIFIED-CONTROLLING through G-GENERAL-NON-RESTRICTED). No free-form injection of trust fields, source content, or arbitrary metadata is accepted from the client -- only a fixtureId string is read, and it must exactly match a registry key.
securityPosture.failsClosedOutsideStaging: resolveStagingFixture() returns null unless isStagingBackendRuntime(env) is true -- the same server-injected-Render-env gate already proven in security/cors-policy.js's CORS remediation, never the client Host header, never NODE_ENV alone.
securityPosture.requiresExistingAuthentication: Wired into ask-handler.js strictly AFTER the existing authenticate middleware / userId check -- no new authentication bypass.
securityPosture.noDataMutationBeyondNormalPersistence: Never calls retrieval or an LLM; writes only the same conversation-message persistence every other /ask response already writes for the authenticated caller's own conversation.
securityPosture.noSecretsOrTaxpayerData: All fixture content is generic, publicly-safe Philippine tax text (NIRC sections, RR/RMC references); no real client or taxpayer information.

frontendAccessMethod: The existing real chat UI: a new '/fixture <FIXTURE-ID>' slash command (src/App.jsx) routes through the normal composer -> /ask flow, typed and sent exactly like every other command, rather than a raw API call bypassing the UI. Harmless if ever reached in production since the backend resolver fails closed there regardless.
unitTestVerification: tests/phase-10a4c-trust-calibration-conflict-accessibility-keyboard-fixture-remediation-1.test.mjs: all A-G fixtures produce exactly their intended canonical trust state (14/14 tests pass); registry fails closed on production and local runtimes; unknown/non-string fixture IDs denied even on staging; no secrets in the module source.
